_note: Descriptions of the gate-level symbols in ND-13.003.01, written from the manual's pictures (cut-outs in catalog/symbols/nd1976/). 'formula' is the manual's printed formula. 'kind' and 'outputType' feed the netlist and the simulator.

7400.description: A plain tall rectangle, empty inside. Inputs enter on the left, one output line leaves the middle of the right side.
7400.tells: Empty box = NAND. No X, no diagonal, no triangle, no second box.

7401.description: The NAND rectangle with one vertical line down the centre of the box, dividing it into two halves.
7401.tells: Centre vertical bar = open collector. Without the bar it is the plain NAND (7400).

7402.description: A rectangle with both diagonals drawn corner to corner (an X filling the box).
7402.tells: X across the whole box = NOR.

7403.description: The NAND rectangle with one vertical line down the centre of the box, dividing it into two halves.
7403.tells: Centre vertical bar = open collector. Without the bar it is the plain NAND (7400). Same symbol as 7401; only the parts list tells 7401 from 7403 (they have different pinouts).

7404.description: A small rectangle with a triangle drawn inside it pointing right: two lines from the left corners meet at the middle of the right side.
7404.tells: Box with an inner right-pointing triangle = inverter.

7405.description: A small rectangle with ONE diagonal, from the bottom left corner to the top right corner. No triangle.
7405.tells: Single diagonal, no triangle = open-collector inverter. Compare 7404 (two lines forming a triangle).

7406.description: A box whose right side is drawn as a point (a pentagon, like a house on its side), with one diagonal inside.
7406.tells: Pointed right end = buffer/driver. Diagonal inside = open-collector, inverting.

7407.description: One rectangle split down the middle: left half empty, right half holds one diagonal from its bottom left corner to the middle of the right edge.
7407.tells: Same split box as the open-collector AND (7409), but one input.

7408.description: One rectangle split down the middle by a vertical line: left half empty, right half holds a triangle pointing right (two lines from its left corners meeting at the middle of the right edge).
7408.tells: Split box with a triangle in the right half = AND. The manual draws AND as NAND followed by an inverter, in one box.

7409.description: One rectangle split down the middle: left half empty, right half holds one diagonal from its bottom left corner up to the middle of the right edge.
7409.tells: Split box with a diagonal (not a triangle) in the right half = open-collector AND.

7410.formula: Y = NOT(A AND B AND C)
7410.description: The empty NAND rectangle with three inputs.

74H11.formula: Y = A AND B AND C
74H11.description: The split AND rectangle (triangle in the right half) with three inputs.

7413.formula: Y = NOT(A AND B AND C AND D)
7413.description: The empty NAND rectangle with four inputs; its top edge runs on to the right and its bottom edge runs on to the left. What a Schmitt trigger is: a normal TTL input switches at one voltage, so a slow or noisy signal near that voltage makes the output flicker between 0 and 1 several times. A Schmitt trigger input has two switching points instead: the input must rise above about 1.7 V before the output changes, and then fall below about 0.9 V before it changes back. The gap between them (the hysteresis) means noise and slow edges give one clean change. It is used on signals from cables, switches and RC delay circuits. The input still reads as plain logic 0 or 1; only its noise tolerance differs.
7413.tells: Edges running past the box (top to the right, bottom to the left) = Schmitt trigger input.

7414.description: The inverter rectangle (triangle inside) with its top edge running on to the right and its bottom edge running on to the left. What a Schmitt trigger is: a normal TTL input switches at one voltage, so a slow or noisy signal near that voltage makes the output flicker between 0 and 1 several times. A Schmitt trigger input has two switching points instead: the input must rise above about 1.7 V before the output changes, and then fall below about 0.9 V before it changes back. The gap between them (the hysteresis) means noise and slow edges give one clean change. It is used on signals from cables, switches and RC delay circuits. The input still reads as plain logic 0 or 1; only its noise tolerance differs.

7416.description: A narrow box with a vertical bar inside, ending in a point on the right.
7416.tells: Same family as 7406 but drawn with a bar instead of a diagonal. The picture is small; confirm with the parts list.

7417.description: Drawn as a whole package: a tall rectangle with six inputs on the left and six outputs on the right.
7417.tells: Package drawing, not a gate symbol.

7420.formula: Y = NOT(A AND B AND C AND D)
7420.description: The empty NAND rectangle with four inputs.

74H21.formula: Y = A AND B AND C AND D
74H21.description: The split AND rectangle (triangle in the right half) with four inputs.

7425.formula: Y = NOT(G AND (A OR B OR C OR D))
7425.description: A tall X box with four inputs, and a fifth input G entering from below the box (strobe).
7425.tells: X box with an input from underneath = NOR with strobe.

7427.formula: Y = NOT(A OR B OR C)
7427.description: The X box with three inputs.

7428.description: The X box ending in a point on the right (pentagon shape).

7430.formula: Y = NOT(A AND B AND C AND D AND E AND F AND G AND H)
7430.description: A very tall empty NAND rectangle with eight inputs.

7432.description: One rectangle split down the middle: X in the left half, triangle in the right half.
7432.tells: Split box, X left, triangle right = OR (NOR followed by an inverter).

7433.description: The X box ending in a point, with a vertical bar between box and point.
7433.tells: X + bar + point = open-collector NOR buffer.

7437.description: An empty box whose right side is a point (pentagon).

7438.description: An empty box, a narrow bar, then a pointed right end.
7438.tells: Bar before the point = open-collector NAND buffer. Compare 7437 (point, no bar).

7440.formula: Y = NOT(A AND B AND C AND D)
7440.description: A tall empty box with a long point on the right, four inputs.

7486.description: A rectangle with a vertical line down the centre and a short equals sign (two short horizontal lines) across that line.
7486.tells: Mark inside the box = exclusive OR.

7450.description: Boxes stacked on the left (the AND parts) feeding an X box (the OR-invert). The manual notes the four-input gates are 7460 circuits (expanders). 7451 is drawn the same way.
7450.tells: Stacked boxes feeding an X box = AND-OR-INVERT.

75150.description: A large open triangle pointing right, inputs A and S on the left.
75150.tells: Big triangle without a box = line driver.

75154.description: A large open triangle pointing right with one input.
75154.tells: Big triangle, one input. The manual heads it 'Line driver'.
